findings.reason: §2 and §6 each declare a control (the three-pitch translation, the corrupted-coefficient mutation) and the plan's own contract requires one, so §3 and §4 need the same clause added before a node is dispatched.
findings.text: §3's done-when ("the private-flux cells book zero plasma current", "the net current matches the analytic total to 1e-12 relative") and §4's done-when (":63", "one compiled program serves two geometries of the same shape") state gates but name no negative control, so neither node can show its guard fires — a run can satisfy every stated clause on a code path that never exercises the guard (a level-test-only booker that books private-flux cells as plasma, or a map that compiles a fresh program per geometry)

findings.reason: a §4/§6 node reading the clause literally would report the map-fidelity gate failed (0.0195 > 1e-2) at the rung the decision just created, or report it passed off an exterior residual that measures the fixture, not the map.
findings.text: §6's acceptance table sets "map fidelity at the analytic state, no solve ≤ 1e-2 relative sup", and §4's done-when repeats "within 1e-2 relative sup at every certificate rung" (":63"), while the analytic certificate row is redefined at "about 2,000, 5,000 and 10,000 cells" (":89") — but the plan's own resolution-strategy evidence records the diverted exact-support map sup as 0.0187 / 0.0195 / 0.0094 at 550 / 2,098 / 5,158 cells (comment c-s21-resolution-pivot-evidence, snapshot line 475; proto-support), i.e. above 1e-2 at the 2,000-cell rung, and followup f-cfs-exterior-on-exact-support states the exterior closure residual (0.006–0.018) still masks the map at those rungs; the sections assert the ≤ 1e-2 bound at 2,000 cells without recording that its satisfaction there depends on that open followup
